title: Clean, lube and adjust the chain
summary: For chain-driven bikes. A clean, oiled chain at the right slack lasts longer and keeps the sprockets from wearing out.
tools: Wrenches for the axle nut and adjusters

steps.text: Put the bike on its center stand so the rear wheel turns freely, with the engine off and the transmission in neutral.
Spray cleaner on a section of the lower run of chain and scrub the plates and rollers with the brush. Turn the wheel by hand and repeat all the way round.
steps.caution: Never turn the wheel with the engine running. A chain can pull in fingers in an instant.

steps.text: Wipe the chain dry with a rag and let any solvent evaporate.
Apply lube to the inside of the chain, where the rollers meet the sprockets, while turning the wheel. Wipe off the excess after ten minutes.
Check the slack midway along the lower run. Most commuters want 20 to 30 mm of up-and-down play.
To adjust, loosen the rear axle nut and turn both adjusters by the same amount so the marks match on each side.
Tighten the axle nut to the torque on your spec sheet, then recheck slack and the rear brake.
steps.caution: If the chain has tight spots or the sprocket teeth look hooked, replace the chain and sprockets together.
